holding_summary: The court affirmed disallowance of a claim for board and lodging furnished to a decedent because the claimant failed to prove how much time the decedent actually lived with him and because the evidence showed the decedent had in fact paid for his board. The court held that no presumption of gratuitous boarding arose merely from the family relationship between the parties, and that recovery, if any, would rest on an implied contract to pay for boarding and lodging furnished.

quotes.text: A claim against a decedent’s estate for board and lodging, furnished to the decedent for a period of three years before his death, will be refused, where the evidence failed to establish how much of the time during the period in question the decedent lived with the claimant, and where there was ample evidence to show that the deceased had paid for his boarding.
The court properly held that the relationship between the decedent and the wife of the claimant did not give rise to a presumption that the boarding was to be furnished gratuitously.
if the claimant was entitled to recovery it was upon an implied contract to pay for the boarding and lodging which he furnished.

notes: Household boarding-for-pay dispute; claim ultimately denied on evidentiary grounds (duration unproven, decedent shown to have paid already), but the legal principle recognized boarding-for-pay as an enforceable implied contract not presumed gratuitous.
Deed-restriction/equity case about converting part of a private dwelling into a real-estate office; no lodging, boarding, or compensated occupancy of rooms at issue.
Criminal conviction for permitting gambling on leased premises operated as a club; leasing of rooms is incidental to the gambling charge, not about lodging/boarding.

holding_summary: The Superior Court reversed the common pleas and upheld a borough ordinance prohibiting street solicitation of patronage for hotels, boarding houses, lodging houses, and garages, holding it a reasonable and valid exercise of the borough's police power.

quotes.text: That no person shall solicit tourists, travelers or other persons to patronize or to do business with any hotel, boarding house, lodging house, garage, or other place for the entertainment of tourists and travelers, upon any of the streets, highways, and other public places within the Borough of Chambersburg.
In this State, boroughs may enact such regulatory ordinances under the police power

notes: Regulation is of street solicitation on behalf of lodging/boarding businesses, not of the letting/occupancy itself, so `characterization` left null — no arrangement between letter and occupant was before the court to classify.

Prohibition-era search-warrant/liquor-possession appeal; defendant's premises are identified in passing as 'a hotel or rooming house,' but the case turns entirely on search-and-seizure law, not letting or lodging.
Nuisance injunction against a public automobile garage in a residential district; no lodging, boarding, or paying-occupant issue.

Ordinary month-to-month house tenancy dispute over notice-to-quit procedure under the Act of 1905; not a boarding/lodging arrangement and does not address the legal character of compensated short-term occupancy.
False-pretense conviction over a fraudulent lease of exhibition floor space in an armory; commercial exhibition space, not dwelling/lodging occupancy.

Township building-code case holding the township lacked authority to require an occupancy certificate before converting office space to apartments; concerns building-code/certificate authority generally, not the legal character of letting/boarding or a paying-occupant dispute.
Commercial storeroom lease dispute over rights to an adjoining sidewalk lunch-counter concession; not a dwelling/lodging matter.

Negligence suit by a tenant's wife over a defective repaired step in a leased dwelling house; ordinary landlord-tenant repair-duty case, does not address the character of letting rooms/lodging for pay.

Divorce/desertion case; mentions of a 'Northside rooming house' and the parties being 'merely boarders' at a son-in-law's house are incidental to the desertion analysis, not about the legal character of letting/boarding.
Divorce/desertion case; a husband's securing of 'furnished rooms' is mentioned only as part of a reconciliation-offer narrative, not a lodging/letting dispute.
Constitutionality of the state Dog License Law; wholly unrelated to lodging or boarding.
Zoning Board of Appeals side-yard variance dispute for a single-family dwelling under construction; no paying-occupant or lodging issue.
Municipal license-fee ordinance for junk dealers upheld under the police power; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.
Real-estate sale dispute over whether a predecessor's wall-building covenant was an encumbrance; no lodging/boarding issue.
Landlord's-warrant/replevin dispute over whether a legal holiday delayed a rent due date; ordinary landlord-tenant procedure, not lodging/boarding.
